newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria pumps cash into firms to save jobs.
newsitem.headline: Algeria pumps cash into firms to save jobs.

text.p: Algeria has injected a total of 67.1 billion dinars ($1.24 billion) into 66 building firms to help them modernise, become more efficient and save the jobs of nearly 127,000 workers, official figures showed on Tuesday.
The Algerian news agency APS said the latest injection of cash totalled 17.4 billion dinars and was made to five firms to safeguard nearly 22,000 jobs.
The five firms, plus a sixth, signed a "performance contract" at the Housing Ministry on Tuesday as part of a deal with the Algerian government giving them more autonomy.
The original agreement was reached last April as part of the authorities' efforts to get state-run industry back on its feet, along with plans for privatisation.

Algeria, battered by violence and sabotage blamed on Moslem fundamentalists, is struggling to move to a free market economy with plans for privatisation and a midway stage of giving some state enterprises more autonomy tied to more responsibility. ($1=5.4 dinars)
